title: Count Subarrays With K Distinct Integers
summary: Given an integer array nums and two integers k and m, count the number of subarrays where the subarray contains exactly k distinct integers and each distinct integer appears at least m times.
statement: Given an integer array nums and two integers k and m, count the number of subarrays where the subarray contains exactly k distinct integers and each distinct integer appears at least m times.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 integers; k and m are positive.
Count contiguous subarrays with exactly k distinct values.
Every one of those distinct values must occur at least m times in the subarray.
hints: Count a difference of two thresholded window families to isolate exactly k distinct values.
For each distinct-count limit, track both map size and how many values have reached frequency m.
Shrink while both thresholds hold; each removed prefix contributes one valid start for the current right endpoint.
Subtracting the k+1-distinct family removes every window with extra values, leaving exactly k whose frequencies all meet m.
editorial: Subtracting the k+1-distinct family removes every window with extra values, leaving exactly k whose frequencies all meet m.

tests.explanation: The qualifying subarrays are [1,2,1,2] and [1,2,1,2,2], giving two.
Only the full array has one distinct value occurring at least twice.
